minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Open Space Committee spent most of the meeting reviewing and voting to approve a draft mission statement, set of goals, and a draft bylaw meant to convert the committee from an ad hoc body to a formally standing committee, with a membership change adding an agricultural commission representative in place of a vacant community seat. The committee voted to send these drafts to the town manager, town council, and the bylaw review committee ahead of spring town meeting; brief reports followed from other boards and no members of the public spoke.

what_happened.line: Committee voted 4-0 to approve a draft bylaw making itself a standing committee, headed to the town manager, town council and bylaw review committee.
Committee voted 4-0 to approve a mission statement and goals, with the chair authorized to present them to the town manager and town council.
The proposal keeps appointments through the planning board rather than the select board, and swaps a vacant community seat for an agricultural commission seat.
Members will research where town bylaws specify who gets notified when land exits Chapter 61 status, aiming to add the committee to that list.
Next Open Space Committee meetings set for December 10, 2025 and January 14, 2026.

why_it_matters: A bylaw creating a standing Open Space Committee, with its membership and duties, would go before voters at spring town meeting.
Formal standing status and a named agricultural seat change who sits on the committee and how it is appointed, affecting town land-use advice going forward.
Getting added to Chapter 61 notifications would let the committee weigh in whenever land exits that reduced-tax farm/forest/open-space status.
